COP commands that change fields of an actor: position, parameters, animation, mirroring, drawing order, palette. Commands (id, uses): 11 MoveActorToTile (32), 12 SetActorResume (10), 13 SetActorParam (0), 17 SetOwnParam (367), 1D SetActorFlags (1), 1E MaskActorFlags (1), 2F ShiftPlayerActors (12), 33 ShowPlayerActors (5), 34 HidePlayerActors (12), 80 SetAnimation (1614), 81 SetAnimationRepeat (522), 82 WaitAnimationDone (1623), 83 WaitAnimationRepeat (529), 87 / 88 ToggleFlipX / Y (45 / 4), 8F / 90 FacePlayerX / Y (3 / 2), 92 StartAnimation (21), 93 StartAnimationCount (0), 94 AnimTick (22), 95 AnimTickRepeat (0), 96-99 SetFlipX / ClearFlipX / SetFlipY / ClearFlipY (226 / 310 / 10 / 14), 9D SetAnimationClearBlocked (51), 9E WaitAnimationDoneOrJumpIfBlocked (51), 9F AddX (79), A0 AddY (39), A1 AddXY (58), A2 SetPriority (54), A3 DrawInFront (121), A4 DrawBehind (34), A5 JumpByFlipState (25), A6 / A7 ClearDrawInFront / Behind (13 / 5), A8 SetAnimationTable (37), A9 SetDynamicTileSource (1), AA SetPalette (11). Conventions shared by all handlers: cop_core block note.

=== FIELDS TOUCHED ===
Actor fields (engine_scheduler_sprites_combat_collision block note): $00/$02 x/y, $16 flags, $18 resume address, $1A attribute flags, $1C OAM attribute (bit 15 flip Y, bit 14 flip X, bits 12-13 priority, bits 9-11 palette), $1E animation id, $20 animation step, $22/$24 animation table and bank, $2A repeat counter, $2C/$34 dynamic-tile bank and source, $30 free parameter word. $1A: $8000 dynamic-tile sprite, $4000 draw in front, $2000 draw behind, $0080 not drawn.

=== ANIMATION COMMANDS ===
Cop80 and its relatives store the animation id in $1E, clear the step $20 and save the address after the command as the resume pointer. Cop82 then calls SetActorAnimFrame once per run: carry clear = a step was loaded, the actor yields and re-runs Cop82 next frame (the resume pointer points at it); carry set = the animation ended, the script goes on. Cop83 repeats the animation $2A times (set by Cop81). Cop92/Cop93/Cop94/Cop95 drive the stepper in lib_animation directly (NextFrameRecord = advance, carry set = finished, CopyFrameData = copies the record's bytes to WRAM bank $7F, a colour animation, OQ-I026-3). Cop9D and Cop9E add the tile-blocked bit: $16 bit 2 is set when the actor ran into a solid tile.

=== SPRITE ATTRIBUTES ===
CopA2 and CopAA do not translate the operand: the byte is the high byte of the attribute, with the bits already in place (priority $10-$30, palette $02-$0E). CopA3/A4/A6/A7 set and clear the draw-order bits that CullAndSortActors turns into sort keys 0 (in front) and $01FE (behind). CopA8 sets the animation table pointer $22 and bank $24 (the effects bank $0E with table $8000 is used by RunAppearPuff); CopA9 turns an actor into a dynamic-tile sprite ($1A bit $8000).

=== PLAYER ACTORS ===
The player is three actors: the player (player_actor $039C), the sword (player_weapon_actor $039E) and the soul orb (soul_orb_actor $03A0). Cop33 / Cop34 clear / set the not-drawn bit on all three and zero / increment player_hidden_count ($0464); while it is non-zero player_core clears joy_pressed. Cop2F moves the player actor and the actor linked at its $3E by a signed amount (used in ms_snow_mountain_actors and gw_lostside_marsh_actors for forced movement of 2 pixels per frame).
cop_conditions:
COP commands that jump on a condition about actors, the player and the screen. Commands (id, uses): 0C JumpIfActorInBox (94), 0D JumpIfActorAtTile (76), 1C JumpIfActorFlags (6), 20 JumpIfPlayerOffGrid (3), 2E JumpIfActorInBoxWord (3), 89 / 8A JumpIfPlayerWithinX / Y (0 / 0), 8B / 8C JumpIfPlayerBeyondX / Y (0 / 0), 8D JumpIfOnScreen (0), 8E JumpIfOffScreen (0), 9A / 9B JumpByPlayerDeltaX / Y (175 / 174), 9C JumpByPlayerAxis (28), AD WaitUntilOnScreen (80). The other conditional jumps are in cop_script_flow_flags (flags, switches), cop_items_stats_text (items, Gems), cop_actor_fields_animation (Cop9E, CopA5) and cop_tiles_spawn_kill (tiles, Cop30).

=== CONVENTIONS ===
A jump command reads the &Code word at the script pointer and leaves through CopExitJump; a failed test leaves through the CopExitSkipN that matches the unread operand bytes (the position and slot operands are consumed first). Actor positions are x (left) and y (bottom edge) in pixels at $00/$02 of the actor; a box is the actor's width $10 and height $12. A tile operand is multiplied by 16 (TileToPixel); because y is the bottom edge, an actor standing on tile row n has y = (n + 1) x 16. Other actors are named by slot number 0-63 (SlotNumberToActor: $0800 + number x $40). player_x and player_y ($0374/$0376) are the player's position.

=== BOX TESTS ===
Cop0C and Cop2E (CopActorBoxTest) test whether the other actor's position lies inside the caller's box widened by a margin m: x in [x - m, x + m + width - 16] and y in [y - m - height + 16, y + m]. Cop0C takes m in tiles, Cop2E in pixels. Lair proximity scripts (RunLairProximity) use Cop0C; Cop0D tests for exactly one tile.

=== THREE-WAY BRANCHES ===
Cop9A and Cop9B take a threshold T and three targets: player left of (above) the actor by more than T, within the band, right of (below) it by T or more. Cop9C compares the X and Y distances to the player. They steer NPCs and enemies toward or away from the player; the usual follow-up is a facing or animation command.

=== UNUSED AND SUSPICIOUS ===
Cop89-Cop8E have no uses (OQ-I025-4). On the not-taken path Cop8D and Cop8E leave through CopExitContinue without skipping the &Code operand, so the script would run the target word as code (OQ-I001-1); harmless while unused. CopAD stops waiting once the actor is on screen or outside the map (it compares the actor position with map_width_px / map_height_px).
cop_core:
CopB2_SpawnBeforeRelative, the exit chain and the helpers shared by every COP handler (file offsets 25715-26309, SNES $00:E473-$E6C5, bank 00). The handlers are in the cop_handlers files: cop_script_flow_flags, cop_items_stats_text, cop_conditions, cop_actor_fields_animation and cop_tiles_spawn_kill; the dispatcher and tables are in cop_dispatch.

=== CONVENTIONS OF EVERY HANDLER ===
HandleCop enters a handler with X = Y = the actor slot, DP $38 = the script pointer just past the id byte (the first operand byte) and DP $3A = the script bank. Every handler starts with TYX, reads its operands with LDA [$38] / INC $38 (a word costs two INCs; a Byte operand is read as a word and masked with $00FF) and leaves through the exit chain with BRL. A and Y are scratch; X is the actor slot again on exit, so the next COP of the script finds it intact. Scratch DP used by handlers: $00, $0C, $0E, $16, $18 (listed in each part note). A script that calls COP from its own code must keep X = actor slot (AGENTS.md, COP register requirement).
A jump command reads the target word and leaves through CopExitJump; a failed condition leaves through the CopExitSkipN that matches the operand bytes still unread. A wait command (Cop05, Cop82, Cop83, CopAD) does not move past itself while the wait lasts: it saves a resume pointer that re-runs the same COP next frame and yields. A command that spawns, kills or changes fields simply continues through CopExitContinue.

=== EXIT CHAIN ===
The chain (CopExitSkip5 .. CopExitYield) is entered by BRL from the handlers: CopExitSkip5 skips 5 operand bytes, CopExitSkip4 skips 4, CopExitSkip3 skips 3, CopExitSkip2 skips 2, CopExitSkip1 skips 1, CopExitContinue skips none. They fall through to CopExitJump, which writes A over the return address on the stack ($02,S) and returns with RTI, so the script continues at A (for a jump, A is the target). CopExitSaveResume stores $38 as the actor's resume pointer ($18,X) and falls into CopExitYield, which pops the COP frame and returns with RTL (yield to the actor loop).

=== FLAGS AND INVENTORY ===
Event flags are a bit array at $1A5E. A flag word has the bit number (0-7) in its low byte and the byte index in bits 8-14; bit 15 is a command-specific sense bit (Cop05_WaitWhileFlagEquals, Cop09_SetOrClearFlag). The inventory/progress bytes are at $1B1E (entry n at $1B1E + n - 1, bit 7 = flag, bits 0-6 = value).

=== ACTORS, TILES, SPAWNING ===
Actor slots are 0x40 bytes wide from $0800. Actors are in a doubly linked list ($3C = next, $3E = previous; heads $06A6 and $06A8). Free slots are kept on a stack addressed by $4A (word entries; a taken entry is zeroed); when it is empty PopFreeSlot returns the scratch slot $06AA with carry set and the spawn handlers, which never test the carry, write into that slot. The spawn helpers link a new actor after (SpawnActorAfter) or before (SpawnActorBefore) the caller and clone the caller's first $3C bytes into it (InitSpawnedActor); the handlers then set the entry address ($18, bank $36) and optionally position and $16. BlockActorFootprint and ClearActorFootprint write the $F0 block mark into tile_type_map ($7F8000) for the box of an actor (width $10, height $12; a box with width + height below $21 is one tile at (x, y - 16)).
cop_dispatch:
COP and BRK dispatchers and the COP command tables (from file offset 22012, SNES $00:D5FC, bank 00).

=== BRK (HandleBrk) ===
BRK #n is the sound request. HandleBrk reads the signature byte n after the BRK (return address minus 1, long pointer in DP $3B-$3D). When bit 6 ($40) of n is set, n and $BF is stored in $0399 (the high byte of the sound word); otherwise n is stored in $0398 (sound_request, the low byte). HandleVBlank writes the word to APUIO2 on even frames and clears it (engine_vblank_nmi, section SOUND). A is preserved; DP $3B-$3D are clobbered. What the two bytes mean to the sound driver is OQ-I024-1. us/config.json lists HandleBrk and HandleCop as the native BRK and COP vectors (nativeBrk, nativeCop).

=== COP (HandleCop) ===
The COP instruction runs actor scripts. HandleCop takes the actor slot from X (TXY), builds the script pointer in DP $38/$3A from the pushed return address (bank byte from $04,S, address $02,S minus 1, so the pointer starts on the COP signature byte), reads the command id, advances $38 and jumps through the word table at CopHandlerTable_00_3C indexed by id*2.

The table has three extracted parts: CopHandlerTable_00_3C (ids 00-3C), CopFillerTable_3D_7F (ids 3D-7F, filler words, no handlers) and CopHandlerTable_80_B2 (ids 80-B2). The ids 0E, 0F, 2C and 2D have no handler (#$0000).

Each handler is a Cop<ID>_<Name> label in extracted/cop_handlers; it ends by jumping into the exit chain in cop_core. Reference: docs/cop/index.md.
cop_items_stats_text:
COP commands for text, menus, items, Gems, EXP and HP. Commands (id, uses): 01 ShowText (608), 02 PromptYesNo (0), 0A GiveItemIfNotOwned (47), 0B RemoveItem (27), 18 JumpIfItemMissing (55), 19 JumpUnlessItemEquipped (36), 1A ChoiceMenu (27), 25 AddGems (0), 26 PayGemsOrJump (8), 36 AddExp (0), 37 HealPlayerToFull (12), 38 QueueExp (13), 39 DamagePlayer (6), 3A EnterPlayerName (1). Conventions shared by all handlers: cop_core block note.

=== INVENTORY ===
The inventory is the byte array inventory ($1B1E); entry n (1-based, the item id) is at $1B1E + n - 1: bits 0-6 hold the value (the entry number itself when owned; the engine's give routine lib_0109D6_part3.StoreInventoryEntry writes it), bit 7 is the 'equipped' flag (OQ-I006-2). cop_core.LookupInventoryEntry reads an entry for Cop0A, Cop0B, Cop18 and Cop19. Ids seen in the scripts: $38 Medical Herb, $39 Strange Bottle, $40 Magic Bell (CheckPlayerDeath, engine_003005), $20-$29 (Cop19 in scene actors; names in plans/doc-audit/walkthrough-crosswalk.md section 4).

=== GEMS, EXP, HP ===
All three counters are BCD. Gems: gems_low ($1B66) and gems_high ($1B68), capped at 999999 by lib_player_stats.AddGems; the price check is SubtractGems (carry set = not enough). EXP: player_exp ($1B78 low word, $1B7A high word). Cop38 does not add EXP directly: it stores the amount in exp_pending ($043D) and the main loop's DrainPendingExp pays it out one digit step per 8 frames with sound. Cop37 sets heal_pending ($043B) = max HP - HP and DrainPendingHeal heals one point every 4 frames. hud_dirty_flags ($0332) bit $04 redraws the HP bar, bit $02 the EXP and bit $10 the Gem counter.

=== TEXT AND MENUS ===
Cop01 passes a 16-bit string pointer in the script bank to lib_text_render.ShowDialogueText (DBR = script bank). Cop1A prints the option text (PrintTextString), runs lib_012281.RunChoiceMenu (A = number of entries; returns the chosen index in A, carry set = cancelled; sound $18 on choosing, $07 on cancelling), redraws (EraseWindowFrame) and stores the index in choice_result ($03D0). The option strings are in shared_choice_prompt_texts (ChoiceYesNoText ' Yes / No' with 2 entries, ChoiceYesOnlyText a single 'Yes', ChoiceRecordMoveQuitText 'Record / Move / Quit' with 3 entries, ChoiceRecordQuitText 'Record / Quit' with 2, ChoiceStayGoBackText 'Stay / Go back' with 2; layout rule in the block note of shared_choice_prompt_texts). Cop3A opens the name-entry screen (lib_name_entry.RunNameEntryScreen, name buffer from $1B92), used once at the start of the game after the Master's speech (the walkthrough: 'you will then get to pick a name for yourself').
cop_script_flow_flags:
COP commands for script flow, event flags, scene changes, randomness and music loading. Commands (id, uses in extracted/ at I025): 00 Yield (0), 03 LoopStart (229), 04 LoopNext (228), 05 WaitWhileFlagEquals (70), 06 Jump (0), 07 JumpIfFlagEquals (190), 08 JumpIfFlagNotEquals (7), 09 SetOrClearFlag (213), 10 SetNextScene (65), 14 JumpIfSwitchSet (245), 1B DelayThenGoto (211), 1F StepRandom (49), 27 YieldThenGoto (81), 31 FadeAndLoadMusic (9), 32 StopAndLoadMusic (5), 35 RandomMod (9), 3B JumpIfSwitchSetElseHold (28), 3C SetTransitionType (23), 91 SetEntryHere (414). Conventions shared by all handlers: cop_core block note.

=== RESUME POINTER AND WAITS ===
An actor script runs when its wait counter $14 goes below 0 (the actor loop in engine_scheduler_sprites_combat_collision decrements it every frame). A yield (CopExitYield, or a plain RTL in the script) returns to the actor loop; the next run starts at the resume address $18,X in the bank $36,X. So a command that must repeat sets or keeps $18,X: Cop91 stores the address after itself (a script that is COP 91 ... RTL re-runs from there every frame), Cop1B stores a target plus a delay in $14 (the script runs delay + 1 frames later), Cop27 stores a target and clears $14 (next frame), Cop03/Cop04 keep a loop start in $2C and a counter in $2E (one loop per actor, no nesting; $2E is also the monsters-left counter of the lair scripts). Cop05 rewinds $38 to the COP instruction itself so the wait re-tests every frame. Two commands in a row, COP 03 (#N) and COP 04 with nothing between, are a pause of N frames.

=== FLAG WORDS AND SWITCHES ===
Event flags (cop_core.TestEventFlag, WriteEventFlag): a word with the bit number in bits 0-7, the byte index into event_flags ($1A5E) in bits 8-14 and a sense bit v in bit 15. Cop05 waits while the flag equals v, Cop07 jumps when it equals v, Cop08 when it differs from v, Cop09 writes v. Switches are a second bit array at $1ADE addressed by the lair record index (LairRecords, 32 bytes per record): Cop14 and Cop3B test them and register the calling actor in switch_owner_table; HoldActorUntilReleased (engine_003005) sets the bits.

=== SCENES, RANDOM, MUSIC ===
Cop10 writes scene_next ($0318; the main loop's loader starts when it is non-zero) and the arrival point warp_dest_*; Cop3C chooses the transition style first. Cop1F and Cop35 are the random pair (state $0302-$0311 of rng_state). Cop31 and Cop32 spawn the music-load actor (MusicLoadSendFade / MusicLoadSendStop in engine_spawn_lairs_death_drops, section MUSIC LOAD AND RESPAWN): the operand is a track number, an index into MusicPointerTable (21 long pointers); the numbers used are $00, $02, $0D, $11, $12 and $13.
cop_tiles_spawn_kill:
COP commands for the tile map, spawning and killing actors. Commands (id, uses): 15 BlockOwnTiles (209), 16 UnblockOwnTiles (82), 21 JumpIfTileAbove (43), 22 JumpIfTileBelow (45), 23 JumpIfTileLeft (50), 24 JumpIfTileRight (47), 28 JumpIfTileHere (24), 29 JumpIfTileIdDiffers (0), 2A BlockTileAt (20), 2B UnblockTileAt (20), AE JumpIfTileTypeNonZero (52), 30 SpawnIfEnteredViaRecord (32), 84 SpawnActorAfter (13), 85 SpawnActorBefore (346), 86 KillSelf (283), AB SpawnAfterAbsolute (0), AC SpawnBeforeAbsolute (38), AF SpawnAfterWithFlags (12), B0 SpawnBeforeWithFlags (76), B1 SpawnAfterRelative (0). CopB2_SpawnBeforeRelative (114) is in cop_core. Conventions shared by all handlers: cop_core block note.

=== TILE MAP ===
tile_type_map ($7F8000) has one byte per 16x16 tile. The low nibble is the tile type (collision), the whole byte is non-zero for a solid tile; blocking an actor's tiles ORs $F0 into the byte (cop_core.BlockActorFootprint) and unblocking zeroes the byte (ClearActorFootprint, Cop2B). lib_map_index_helpers.PixelToMapIndex turns the pixel position in dp$16 (x) and dp$18 (y) into the byte index. y is the bottom edge of an actor, so the row the actor stands on is y - 16: Cop28 samples (x, y - 16), Cop21 (x, y - 16 - height) above the box, Cop22 (x, y) below it, Cop23 (x - 16, y - 16) left of it and Cop24 (x + width, y - 16) right of it. Cop21-Cop24 and Cop28 jump when the whole byte is non-zero (a block mark or a type); CopAE tests only the type nibble and takes its position relative to the actor. Cop2A/Cop2B use the same relative offsets. Cop29 (unused) compares the byte at $7E8000 + index with an operand.

=== SPAWNING ===
Operands: 84 / 85: @Code (word + bank byte); AF / B0: @Code, Word flags ($16); AB / AC: @Code, Word x, Word y, Word flags; B1 / B2: @Code, Word dx, Word dy, Word flags (position = the caller's plus the offset); 30: Word record index, @Code. Every variant allocates with SpawnActorAfter / SpawnActorBefore, which clone the caller (InitSpawnedActor), then store the entry in $18 and the bank in $36 and, depending on the variant, overwrite position and $16. With an empty free-slot stack the new actor lands in the scratch slot $06AA and nothing is linked (the handlers do not check the carry). Cop30 spawns only for a visit that began at lair record N: return_active ($03FB) non-zero and return_record ($0405, stored by the return-trip warp in lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return) equal to the operand.

=== KILL ===
Cop86 unlinks the caller from the actor list ($3C next, $3E previous; heads $06A8 / $06A6) and pushes its slot on the free-slot stack. The script keeps running after the COP, which is why every kill is followed by RTL.
data_chest_lists:
Chest lists: the 128-word pointer table by location_id and the lists of 6-byte chest rows (file offsets 43486-44181, SNES $01:A9DE-$AC95, bank 00; 256 + 440 bytes).

=== MODEL ===
TryOpenChest (lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return) and the scene init code in lib_scene_map_patches read chest_list_ofs, the list of the current location, which the scene loader takes from ChestListPointers[location_id x 2]. A chest is not an actor: the map holds the chest tile ($FB closed, $FC open) and the list says which tile belongs to which chest, what it holds and which bit of the chest array remembers that it was opened.
Row (6 bytes): +0 x, +1 y of the tile the player stands on (the chest tile is one above, y - 1); +2 chest id (bits 0-6 = the bit number in the array $1A7E, bit 7 = the tile is also edited on BG2); +3 content (0 empty, $FF Gems, any other value an inventory entry); +4 word Gem amount (BCD, little-endian: the bytes 12 00 are 12 Gems). A list ends with $FF.

=== WHAT IS HERE ===
97 of the 128 location ids have a list; the 31 ids without a scene (25-27, 35-3B, 48-4F, 5D-63, 74-77, 7E, 7F) hold $0000. Of the 97, 60 share ChestListEmpty (a single $FF byte) and 37 have their own label: 36 with chests (67 chests in all: 1 to 4 per room) and ChestListLoc0A, an empty list of its own (Tulip's Dream) that duplicates the shared one. Names are ChestListLocLL with LL = location_id in hex.
Locations with chests (ROM location names): 03 Treasure room, 05 and 06 the Underground Castle, 08 Leo's Paintings, 0D Trial room, 15 Woods of GreenWood, 16 A mole's hole, 1A-1C Water Shrine, 1D-1F Fire Shrine, 20 Light Shrine, 29 Seabed Sanctuary, 2B Secret Cave, 2E Southerta, 2F Shore reef of Rockbird, 30 Durean, 32 A ghost ship, 34 Seabed of St. Elles, 3E Mountain North slope, 3F Aurora's Ridge, 47 Ice field of Laynole, 51 Leo's Laboratory, 58 the power plant, 5B and 5C Model of a town, 66 the torture chamber, 67 and 68 the castle basement, 6E and 6F the right tower, 79 and 7A World of Evil, 7B Dazzling Space.
Checked against the walkthrough: the chest of the Trial room (ChestListLoc0D) holds item 1, the Sword of Life (01-in-the-beginning.md); the chest in the Underground Castle (ChestListLoc05) holds the 12 Gems of 02-grass-valley.md.

=== NOTES ===
- The bit number is a 7-bit value, so a chest id is below 128; $1A7E lies inside the first switch array ($1A5E + $20) and is the chest-opened array.
data_engine_tables:
Engine tables: 16 small tables read all over the engine (file offsets 63991-65091, SNES $01:F9F7-$FE43, bank 00; 1101 bytes).

=== WHAT IS HERE ===
Menu positions: WeaponIconPositions, ArmorIconPositions, MagicIconPositions (8 words each: the BG offsets of the icons of the equipment page) and ItemIconPositions (40 words: the item grid), read by DrawEquipIconRows and DrawItemIconGrid.
Bit and direction tables: SwitchBitMasks (8 bytes $01-$80: the mask of bit n and 7 for every bit array), PlayerFacingByAnim and PlayerMoveDirByAnim (44 bytes each, by the player's animation id: 0 up, 1 down, 2 right, 3 left; ids $2C and up are not valid), WeaponYOffsetByAnim (44 words: the weapon sprite's y offset by animation, 0 or 1 pixel).
Colour and music: GaugeColorLadder (13 BGR555 words: the colour of the HP and enemy gauge in steps of 10 units, dark blue below 50 up to white from 100), MusicPointerTable (21 long pointers to the song data), MagicGraphicsPointers (8 long pointers into graphics_07B000) and MagicPalettePointers (8 long pointers into palette_07D000, 32 bytes each).
Level-up and geometry: LevelExpThresholds (51 rows of 2 BCD words), SineTable plus SineTableTail (one 320-byte signed sine) and CircleHalfWidths (128 bytes).

=== NOTES ===
- The file keeps the extraction's split of the sine (SineTable 64 bytes, SineTableTail 256 bytes): they are one table and the split is only a boundary of the extraction.
- Each part note names its consumers.
data_exit_lists:
Exit lists: the 128-word pointer table by location_id and 97 lists of 11-byte exit rows (file offsets 44182-46745, SNES $01:AC96-$B699, bank 00; 256 + 2308 bytes).

=== MODEL ===
CheckExitRegions (lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return) runs every frame with exit_list_ofs, the list of the current location, which the scene loader takes from ExitListPointers[location_id x 2]. An exit is a rectangle of tiles; when the player stands inside it (the tile inside, then the pixel position inside the rectangle shrunk by 15 pixels) the scene change starts: area_next, scene_next, warp_dest_anim, warp_dest_x and warp_dest_y are stored and the transition begins. So doors, room edges, ladders and portals are data, not scripts.
Row (11 bytes): +0 x, +1 y, +2 width, +3 height (tiles), +4 area_next, +5 scene_next, +6 warp_dest_anim, +7 word warp_dest_x, +9 word warp_dest_y (pixels). A list ends with $FF. Example: the Trial room list holds one row, x 4, y 10, 1 x 1 tiles, to area 0 scene 1, animation 3, at (96, 96).

=== WHAT IS HERE ===
97 of the 128 ids have a pointer (the 31 without a scene hold $0000, as in the chest table). 78 lists have rows (201 in all; 21 lists have 1 row, 28 have 2, 15 have 3, 5 have 4, 2 have 5, 4 have 6, 2 have 7 and 1 has 11), 18 lists are a single $FF byte and one more (ExitListUnreferenced) is empty and not referenced. Names are ExitListLocLL with LL = location_id in hex.
The 18 empty lists are the places the player leaves by a script, not by walking: the dream rooms (0A Tulip's, 0E Lisa's, 23 Bird's, 24 Stump's, 2D the dolphin's, 33 Servas', 40 the old man's, 43 the mushroom's, 55 the cat's, 69 and 73 the soldier's: 'A dream 1' and the others), the five intro scenes 0F-13, 72 the deck (the Demon Falcon's room) and 7D the battle with Deathtoll.

=== NOTES ===
- Location 5A (the second room the ROM calls 'A dream 1') points at the list of location 56 (ExitListLoc56, two rows to area $0D scene 1 and area $0E scene 2), while the empty list ExitListUnreferenced right after ExitListLoc59 has no reader. Every other dream room has an empty list, so the pointer looks like a slip (OQ-I033-5).
- structs.json declares the exit row as 11 Bytes; +7 and +9 are 16-bit reads (retype proposal in FM-A11 4.17).
data_lair_formations:
Lair formations: the 112-word pointer table and 112 lists of 6-byte monster rows (file offsets 61070-63897, SNES $01:EE8E-$F999, bank 00; 224 + 2604 bytes; 434 rows).

=== MODEL ===
RunLairFormation (the script of 107 lair records) places all monsters of a lair at once instead of one after the other. The index is in the lair actor's $26 (the record's +14); the list is the word at FormationPointers + $26 x 2. For each of the lair's monsters (count in $0C, the live count taken from the record's +13) it reads one row: word x, word y, word flip bits (ORed into $1C after AND $3FFF) and spawns the monster at that position with no appear puff.
Rows (6 bytes): +0 word x, +2 word y (pixels), +4 word OR bits for $1C (flip bits $4000 and $8000, so a formation can be mirrored). Lists have no terminator: the monster count ends the walk, so every list must have at least as many rows as the lair has monsters.

=== NOTES ===
- The 112 lists keep their auto names (unk9_00EF6E ...): they are named by index in FormationPointers ($00-$6F), which is what the lair records use.
- Check: 224 + 434 x 6 = 2828 bytes.
data_lair_records:
Lair and release records: 420 records of 32 bytes and a $FF terminator (file offsets 47629-61069, SNES $01:BA0D-$EE8D, bank 00; 13441 bytes). The record index is the switch number of the whole game.

=== MODEL ===
A Monster Lair is a patch of the map ($FD intact, $FE green switch, $FF cleared) that spits out monsters; killing them all opens the switch, and stepping on it releases something: an NPC that goes home (the walkthrough: 'the switch beneath the lair will release the tool shop's owner') or a stretch of map (a path opens). One record describes both halves: where the lair is and what it spawns (+B..+15), and what the release does (+0..+A, +E, +F, +1D, +1E). Record n is also switch n: bit n of the switch array $1ADE and of the released array $1A9E, and byte n of lair_state ($7F0203 + n) is its monster counter. The records are not sorted by location.

=== RECORD (32 bytes) ===
+0 home location (where the released NPC lives; $FF/$80+ ends the table) | +1 slab number (0-3, the alternative map copy shown by the release) | +2, +3 home tile x, y | +4, +5 rectangle x, y (metatiles) | +6, +7 rectangle width, height (0 / 0 writes one type-1 tile) | +8 layer (non-zero: BG2 as well) | +9 name index (the NPC's name in NpcNameStrings) | +A low bits of lair_state after the release ($80 path, $C0 NPC) | +B lair location | +C, +D lair tile x, y (the switch appears here) | +E, +F staging rectangle x, y | +10 word script, +12 script bank (@Code) | +13 monster count (the initial lair_state) | +14 spawn interval (RunLairRespawn, RunLairSpawnAll: $14 = 3 x $26 - 1) or formation index (RunLairFormation: $26 x 2 into FormationPointers) | +15 meta type | +16 word attribute bits ($4000, $8000 or $C000: flips) | +18, +1A words, +1C byte: always 0, no reader | +1D warp_dest_anim | +1E word gate switch (a bit of $1ADE; 0 = none).
The first 8 bytes (+0..+7) are copied by MVN to $1C6D-$1C74 (release_slab, release_npc_x/y, release_rect_x/y/w/h) when a release runs. +E / +F both 0 means the lair frees an NPC; otherwise it opens a path.

=== WHAT IS HERE ===
Scripts: 156 RunLairRespawn, 139 RunLairSpawnAll, 107 RunLairFormation, 8 RunLairProximity, 7 RunLairSpawnAllFlipping and 3 records without a script (monster count 0): records $32, $74 and $75, whose home and lair location is a dream room (0E Lisa's, 23 Bird's, 24 Stump's): switches that no lair actor ever drives.
15 records are identical fillers: home and lair location $63 (a location without a scene), count 1, interval 1, meta type $FF, RunLairRespawn: $26, $27, $2D, $35, $104-$108, $12B, $12C, $146, $156, $157 and $194. Nothing finds them (no scene has location $63), so they only keep the numbering of the switches.
The record index is the switch number everywhere: placement scripts test switch n with COP 14 and COP 3B (HoldActorUntilReleased waits for the lair of record n), and SceneVariantRules names six boss lairs by their index.
Walkthrough check (record $09, the first boss lair): home location 04 (the village chief's room), lair location 0C (Monster in the paintings), lair tile (2, 3), RunLairFormation, 1 monster of meta type $1F (the Metal Mantis, MetaGrassValley). The walkthrough 02-grass-valley.md: 'After beating the Metal Mantis, go onto the northwestern switch that was once underneath the monster lair. You'll end up freeing the village chief'. The other five boss lairs are records $50 (home 15, lair location 22, three Elemental Statues, type $3D), $B6 (home 29, lair 32, Floating Skull, type $41), $103 (home 3D, lair 44, Poseidon, type $38), $12F (home 53, lair 59, Tin Doll, type $1E) and $195 (home 65, lair 72, Demon Falcon, type $09).
Record $00 (home and lair location 0D, the Trial room): 4 monsters of meta type $20, RunLairRespawn.

=== NOTES ===
- Consumers: SpawnLairActor and ApplyLairStatesToScene (spawn and state replay), SealLair, ReleaseLairAtSwitch, PlayLairReleaseScene and RunLairReleaseOnReturn (release), TriggerVariantPlate (plates), HoldActorUntilReleased and Cop3B_JumpIfSwitchSetElseHold (the freed NPCs), InitFixedState (copies +13 to $7F0203 + n).
- structs.json declares unk8 with 16 Bytes, @Code, 3 Bytes and 5 Words; +14 is a byte and +1D a byte read (retype proposal in FM-A11 4.17).
- The existing note of RunLairRespawn says '156 of the 417 lair records': 417 is the number of records that have a script.
data_plate_lists:
Plate lists: the 256-word pointer table and 6 lists of 4-byte pressure plate rows, plus the shared empty list (file offsets 46746-47628, SNES $01:B69A-$BA0C, bank 00; 512 + 371 bytes).

=== MODEL ===
A pressure plate is a tile that switches a room between two map variants after a lair was released. TriggerVariantPlate (lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return) reads plate_list_ofs, which the scene loader takes from the word at ($03AA = location_id x 4) + plate_variant x 2 of this table; plate_lists_ofs keeps the address of the pair. The index is therefore location_id x 2 + variant (0 or 1): the two lists of a pair are the plates of variant 0 and variant 1, and stepping on an active plate of the current variant applies the lair record's slab and toggles the variant, so the next plate takes over.
Row (4 bytes): +0 x, +1 y of the plate tile, +2 word lair record index (the bit number in the released array $1A9E: the plate is inactive until that lair has been released). A list ends with $FF.

=== WHAT IS HERE ===
Only three rooms have plates: location 01 (Grass Valley, the highlands: PlateListLoc01V0 with 17 rows and PlateListLoc01V1 with 12), location 29 (the Seabed Sanctuary: V0 with 19 rows, V1 with 10) and location 65 (the Castle of King Magridd: V0 with 23 rows, V1 with 10). The rows of one list name only a few lair records (for example PlateListLoc01V0 uses records 2 and 6 in its first rows). 188 of the 256 words point to PlateListEmpty (one $FF byte), 62 are $0000 (the 31 ids without a scene, two words each) and 6 point to the lists above.
data_scene_placements:
Scene placement tables: the index of 97 scenes and the 97 actor lists it points to (file offsets 39348-43485, SNES $01:99B4-$A9DD, bank 00; 389 + 3749 bytes).

=== MODEL ===
SpawnSceneActors scans ScenePlacementIndex for the first 4-byte row whose area and scene equal area_current and scene_current (a first byte of $80 or more ends the scan) and hands the row's list to SpawnPlacementList. A scene is one row; the 97 rows are exactly the 97 scenes of the scene profile list (lib_scene_profile_data) and of the asset list (SceneAssetLists, minus its dummy first record).

=== ROWS ===
Index row (4 bytes): +0 area, +1 scene, +2 word &list. List row (4 bytes): +0 x tile, +1 y tile, +2 flags byte (bits 7 and 6 flip Y and X; bit 0 is passed to $1C as $0100), +3 meta type (WorldMetaPointers). Position = x tile x 16, y tile x 16 + 16. A list ends with a byte of $FF. The first row of every list is the hero (meta type 0): its tile is the start position of the scene when no warp_dest is set.
913 rows in all (97 hero rows and 816 actors); the longest list is PlacementA06S01 with 33 rows. The lists are named PlacementAaaSss after the (area, scene) of their index row, both in hex: PlacementA05S02 is area 5, scene 2.

=== AREAS ===
22 areas ($00-$15) with 13, 4, 3, 6, 6, 10, 1, 5, 4, 2, 1, 7, 3, 5, 5, 2, 1, 4, 7, 3, 3 and 2 scenes. docs/areas-and-scenes.md names them and maps (area, scene) to the location_id used by the chest, exit and plate lists.

=== NOTES ===
- Lair monsters are not listed here: they come from LairRecords (the lair actor spawns them), so the 'enemies' of a scene are the placement list plus the lairs of its location.
- structs.json names the index row unk1 and the list row unk2; the 97 lists keep the unk2 type with the delimiter $FF.
data_scene_variant_rules:
Scene variant rules: 23 rows of 4 bytes and a terminator (file offsets 63898-63990, SNES $01:F99A-$F9F6, bank 00; 93 bytes).

=== MODEL ===
LookupSceneVariant (lib_scene_map_patches) is called by ApplySceneProfile when scene_variant is still 0. It walks this table for a row of the current location whose switch bit is set in the switch array $1ADE and, if there is one, stores the row's variant in scene_variant ($031E). The variant picks the music of the scene (the music commands of the asset list carry a variant byte).
Row (4 bytes): +0 location_id (a first byte of $80 or more ends the table), +1 word switch number (a bit of $1ADE), +3 variant. The switch numbers are lair record indices (LairRecords): the six values are the boss lairs, one per world: $0009 the Metal Mantis (world 0), $0050 the Elemental Statues (1), $00B6 the Floating Skull (2), $0103 Poseidon (3), $012F the Tin Doll (4) and $0195 the Demon Falcon (5). The record of each switch has the world's boss as its monster (meta type $1F, $3D, $41, $38, $1E, $09).

=== ROWS ===
Rows per world: world 0 locations 01, 02, 03, 04 (variant 2) and 0C (variant 0); world 1 locations 15, 16, 17, 18 (variant 2) and 22 (0); world 2 locations 29, 2C (2) and 32 (0); world 3 locations 3D (2) and 44 (0); world 4 locations 51, 52, 53, 54 (2) and 59 (0); world 5 locations 65 (2), 72 (0) and 71 (1). The variant-0 rows are the six boss rooms, the rooms whose scene profile adds 2 to the variant (byte 11 = $C0-$C5, lib_scene_profile_data): after the boss lair is released the boss room goes back to variant 0 and the other rooms of the world change to variant 2 (the Castle of King Magridd's dock, 71, to variant 1). The story that fits: the boss music of the room before the boss falls and the music of the world after it (inferred; OQ-I011-5). World 6 has no row.

=== NOTES ===
- Bit n of $1ADE is set by the release code (ReleaseLairAtSwitch for a path, PlayLairReleaseScene for an NPC, which runs once the player has returned to the NPC's home scene), so the rooms change after the release, not at the moment the boss dies.
engine_003005:
Player death check, held-until-released actors, the Soul of Shield sweep and the boss map patch (file offsets 12293-12716, SNES $00:B005-$B1AC, bank 00).

=== DEATH CHECK ===
CheckPlayerDeath runs every frame from RunMainLoop. While the player actor is not yet dying ($16 bit $0400 clear) and player_hp and heal_pending are both 0 it tests three equipped items in this order (Cop19 reads the inventory entry id, bit 7 = equipped, OQ-I006-2): Medical Herb ($38): heal_pending = player_max_hp, the entry is removed (Cop0B) and the player lives. Strange Bottle ($39): the entry is removed and the player dies with his Gems. Magic Bell ($40): not removed, the player dies with his Gems (OQ-I006-1: the walkthrough says the Bottle keeps the Gems and says nothing about the Bell). No item: gems_low and gems_high = 0 and the player dies. 'Dies' is MarkPlayerDead: $16 bit $0400 set and $0800 cleared, joy_block_mask = $2080 (Select/X and A), player_died + 1; the player's own script then runs PlayPlayerDeath (player_core).

=== HELD ACTORS ===
HoldActorUntilReleased is the tail of about a dozen NPC and object scripts (entered by an RTS trick pushed by the actor): the actor blocks its own tiles (COP 15), plays animation 0D and waits until the release switch of its lair record (+$1E of LairRecords, record index in $34, bit array at $1ADE) is set. Then it frees its tiles (COP 16), sets the bits in the arrays at $1A9E and $1ADE, clears bit $40 of lair_state[$34] and becomes the actor of its meta entry (animation, banks, flags, script, SetActorAnimFrame). The walkthrough's 'the switch beneath the lair releases the old woman / the tool shop owner' is this routine.

=== SOUL OF SHIELD ===
DestroyHazardsNearOrb is spawned by lib_0116C3 (souls_flags bit $0004, the Soul of Shield per OQ-I006-10) with flags $2010 and runs every frame: every actor whose $16 is exactly $0301 inside a box of +-$30 pixels around soul_orb_actor gets the script RunHazardPuff and a $14 of 0, so it bursts. The walkthrough says the Shield soul protects from the magma bombs on Durean (the link between the $0301 actors and those bombs is inferred).

=== BOSS MAP PATCH ===
RunBossMapPatch is spawned (COP 85) by five boss scripts (gv_boss_metal_mantis, gw_boss_light_water_fire_statues, ms_boss_poseidon, ll_boss_tin_doll, we_deathtolls_shrine_actors), which set the patch id (0-4) in $30 of the new actor. It blocks all buttons (joy_block_mask = $FFFF), waits one frame, then ApplyBossMapPatch waits for an empty VRAM write queue, plays BRK #$83, calls lib_0108BB.ApplyMapPatchRect with the id and ReleaseInputAndKill clears the mask and ends the actor. Whether the patch closes or opens the boss room is OQ-I024-3.
engine_boot_main_loop:
Reset, main loop and sub-frame runners (file offsets 0-516, SNES $00:8000-$8204, bank 00).

=== FRAME MODEL ===
BootGame (the reset vector) sets native mode, D = 0, S = $1FFF and DBR = $01, runs the hardware init (InitHardwareAndClearWram), ApplyBootPpuLayout, InitFixedState and ClearBg3Buffer (BG3 tilemap buffer), sets scene_next = $000C (scene 0C of area 0, the boot scene), enables NMI, calls the scene loader once and falls into RunMainLoop.

One pass of RunMainLoop is one game frame (location_id not $10-$12 and the low byte of return_active zero):
  1. WaitVBlank: NMI is on, so HandleVBlank runs inside this wait.
  2. Scene loader ChangeSceneIfRequested, only when the low byte of scene_next is non-zero; it runs its own frames through RunSubFrameLoader.
  3. DispatchFieldButtons (Select or X: equipment menu; B: talk to the actor in front; A without a direction: status and souls screen) and pause HandlePauseBanner (Start), NMI still on.
  4. DisableNmi: everything below is the work phase and runs with NMI off.
  5. CheckPlayerTileTriggers (lair switch, pressure plate, chest and exit regions under the player), ResetHdmaQueue (per-frame reset: HDMA shadow dp$42 = 0 and dp$44-dp$48).
  6. RunActors, CullAndSortActors, DetectHitSourceCollisions, DetectPlayerContact, CheckPlayerDeath (death check and automatic Medical Herb), ScrollCameraByDelta and BuildScrollStrips (scroll), BuildOamFromActors.
  7. HUD (UpdateHud, which skips locations $0F-$12 entirely, including the heal and EXP drains; code_011695), QueueAnimatedTileStrip (queues one animated tile strip), EnableNmi, back to step 1.

=== VARIANTS ===
RunReducedLoop: location_id $10-$12 (unnamed scenes of the Up Above area, OQ-I001-6; the boot scene 00/0C should be location $12, OQ-I005-21). Runs DisableNmi, ResetHdmaQueue, RunActors, CullAndSortActors, BuildOamFromActors and EnableNmi only: no menu, no hit tests, no HUD.
RunReturnLoop: low byte of return_active non-zero. Same as the main loop without menu, hit tests and scroll update, and Start, Select and X are cleared; after one frame it loops over RunSubFrame (WaitReturnDone) while bit 7 of $03FC is set, then adds player_max_hp / 8 to heal_pending, calls WaitFrames with A = $78, sets transition_type = $80, copies return_area, return_scene, return_x and return_y into area_next, scene_next, warp_dest_x and warp_dest_y, enables NMI and jumps back to RunMainLoop (OQ-I005-17).

=== SUB-FRAMES ===
RunSubFrameLoader, RunSubFrameMapSweep and RunSubFrame run one complete game frame from inside a script, a menu, the text renderer or the scene loader. They set subframe_active ($03A6) to 1 while the work phase runs: RunActorList then runs only actors whose $16 bit $0010 is set, so a modal routine keeps its own actors alive while the rest of the game stands still. The player actor code and w2_actor_0FA6F5 also read $03A6.

=== WRAM ===
return_active $03FB (word read, low byte = flag), return_area $03FD, return_scene $03FF, return_x $0401, return_y $0403; scene_next $0318 (word) and area_next $0319; warp_dest_x $037C, warp_dest_y $037E; transition_type $03E3; heal_pending $043B; subframe_active $03A6; scene_loading $0462 (HUD skipped while non-zero in RunSubFrameLoader).

=== NOTES ===
- The three RunSubFrame* routines differ only in setup: RunSubFrameLoader disables NMI itself, calls the camera update AimCameraAtPlayer and skips the HUD while scene_loading is set; RunSubFrameMapSweep and RunSubFrame expect NMI off and set DBR = $01 (OQ-I005-20 asks whether every caller guarantees that).
- The extractor decodes BuildScrollStrips with the wrong M flag (OQ-I026-1); the callers run with M = 1. ResetHdmaQueue had the same fault until the M override at 71774 (OQ-I005-7).
engine_scheduler_sprites_combat_collisio:
Actor scheduler, draw list sort, OAM builder, animation, combat and tile collision (file offsets 1445-4782, SNES $00:85A5-$92AD, bank 00).

=== ACTOR SLOTS ===
64 slots of $40 bytes at $0800 + $40 x n. Free slots sit on a stack at $1800-$187F (dp$4A points to it). Two links: run order is from actor_list_tail ($06A6) following $3E; the cull and sort pass goes from actor_list_head ($06A8) following $3C. A new actor is linked in as the new head.
Fields: $00 x, $02 y (words); $04 dx, $06 dy; $08 $0A $0C $0E extent box (left, top, right, bottom distances from x, y); $10 width, $12 height; $14 wait counter; $16 flags; $18 script resume address and $36 its bank; $1A attribute flags; $1C OAM attribute (bit 15 flip Y, bit 14 flip X); $1E animation id; $20 animation step; $22 animation table pointer; $24 data bank of the animation and spritemap data; $25 HP; $26 hit-stun counter; $28 spritemap pointer; $2C and $34 dynamic-tile bank and source; $2E $2F lair state copies; $30 projectile damage ($FF always kills); $38 meta entry pointer; $3A placement record pointer; $3C $3E links.

=== FLAGS ===
$16: $8000 off screen (set by CullAndSortActors and at spawn); $4000 pickup; $2000 hidden or inactive; $1000 runs tile collision; $0800 hit stun; $0400 dying; $0080 hit source (player side) or the player; $0020 projectile; $0010 runs during sub-frames; $0004 blocked by a tile; $0002 deflects hits; $0001 no enemy gauge. Read but unexplained: $0008, $0040, $0100, $0200 (OQ-I005-14).
$1A: $8000 dynamic-tile sprite; $4000 draw in front; $2000 draw behind; $0080 not drawn; $0040 frozen while stunned; $0100 survives lethal hits with 1 HP; $0200, $0400, $0800 immunity classes (special, metal, spirit; see COMBAT).

=== SCHEDULER ===
RunActors pushes EndRunActors - 1 and RunActorList - 1 and executes RTS: RunActorList starts with A = actor_list_tail, and when the list ends its RTS lands in EndRunActors, which restores dp$38-$3A, DBR and P and returns with RTL. RunActorList calls an actor script by pushing a bank-0 return address (StepActorMotion - 1), the script bank ($36) and $18 - 1, then RTL; the script returns with RTL into StepActorMotion with X = slot. A script runs when its wait counter $14 goes below 0. While subframe_active is set only actors with $16 bit $0010 run.

=== DRAW LIST ===
CullAndSortActors sets $16 bit $8000 for actors whose extent box misses the 256 x 224 screen and clears it for the rest, and builds the sorted draw list at $1900 (slot words, 0 ends). Key = (255 - (y - scroll_y)) x 2, so lower actors on screen sort first; key 0 for $1A bit $4000 (in front) and for actors with y - scroll_y outside 0-$FF; key $01FE for $1A bit $2000 (behind). Hidden ($16 bit $2000) and not-drawn ($1A bit $0080) actors are not listed. Bucket sort: pass 1 stores (key, slot) pairs at $1900, pass 2 pops them with S moved to $18FF into 256 linked buckets at $0100-$02FF (nodes carved from the OAM area at $0486), pass 3 pops the bucket heads with S = $00FF and writes the slots back to $1900 in key order, clearing every head with PHA/PLA (A = 0 over the popped word). The scan stops at the $FFFF end marker at $0300 (OQ-I013-1). S relocation is safe only because NMI is off in the work phase (OQ-I005-20).

=== OAM ===
BuildOamFromActors fills the OAM low table ($0486-$0685, 4 bytes per sprite: x, y, tile, attribute) and the high table ($0686-: two bits per sprite, x bit 8 and size) from the draw list through BuildActorSprites, until the list ends or all 128 sprites are used. Unused sprites are set to $E080 (off screen). A spritemap is a word entry count followed by 7-byte entries: flags (bit 0 = size bit), x offset, x offset when flipped in x, y offset, y offset when flipped in y, word tile and attribute (XOR $1C, or $0E00 while the stun flashes). Dynamic-tile actors ($1A bit $8000) copy tile blocks of 32 bytes at source + tile x 32 through tile_dma_list and use OAM tile numbers 0, 2, 4 and so on; the NMI uploads them.

=== ANIMATION ===
SetActorAnimFrame: $22 points to a word table indexed by the animation id; each entry points to a list of 8-byte steps indexed by $20: word duration (negative ends the animation), word dx, word dy, word frame pointer. A frame record has six words (left, right, top, bottom extents, width, height) followed at +12 by the spritemap. Flip bits of $1C negate dx and dy and mirror the extents.

=== COMBAT ===
DetectHitSourceCollisions pairs every listed actor with $16 bit $0080 (and none of $0D00) against every actor without $EEC0 whose box overlaps and whose sprite rectangles overlap (TestSpriteOverlap); sources with $16 bit $0020 go to ApplyProjectileHit, the others to ApplySwordHit. DetectPlayerContact tests the player's hurt box against actors without $25C0 and calls ApplyContactDamageOrPickup. The rules below are read from the code; the item names are those of the walkthrough (docs/walkthrough/items.md).
- Equipment ids: equipped_weapon $1B5E (2 Psycho Sword, 3 Critical Sword, 5 Zantetsu Sword, 6 Spirit Sword, 7 Recovery Sword, 8 Soul Blade), equipped_armor $1B60 ($0D Mystic Armor, $0E Light Armor), equipped_magic $1B62 ($18 Phoenix), equipped_bracelet $1B64 ($35 Power, $36 Shield, $37 Super).
- Sword damage = max(1, attack_current $1B8C - monster defence (meta entry +1)); Power and Super Bracelet double it. Monster HP is $25; a hit that does not leave HP above 0 kills (or leaves 1 HP when $1A bit $0100).
- Immunity classes ($1A): $0400 metal is hurt only by the Zantetsu Sword, $0800 spirit only by the Spirit Sword, $0200 special only by the Soul Blade (which hurts everything). Metal deflects with sound $4C, the other two ignore the hit silently.
- Damage to the player = max(1, monster attack - 1 - defense_current $1B8E); Shield and Super Bracelet halve it. Light Armor blocks the hit when attack x 1.5 is below $1B8E (sound $0C). Mystic Armor sets the hit stun counter to -64 instead of -32.
- Hit stun: $26 = -8 for monsters, $FFE0 or $FFC0 for the player; while $16 bit $0800 is set the stunned player only picks things up.
- Differences from the walkthrough are in OQ-I005-1 (Super Bracelet), -2 (Critical Sword), -3 (Psycho Sword).

=== COLLISION ===
MoveActorWithTileCollision moves x first (CollideEast or CollideWest), then y (CollideSouth or CollideNorth), each probing the tile types in the rows or columns the actor's width and height cover. GetTileType reads tile_type_map ($7F8000): index = ((y / 16) x map_width_pages + x / 16) x 256 + (y and 15) x 16 + (x and 15) for tile coordinates; a type byte with a high nibble set (Cop15_BlockOwnTiles ORs $F0) or an index of $4000 or more reads as $0F (blocked). Blocked: $00 or $02 snapped to a multiple of 16, velocity zeroed, $16 bit $0004 set. Tile type codes are in OQ-I005-8; the east and south routines have no boundary pre-check (OQ-I005-12).

=== ENEMY GAUGE ===
A hit on a monster without $16 bit $0001 sets enemy_gauge_hp ($0336) to its HP, enemy_gauge_max ($0338) to the meta entry HP (+2) and enemy_gauge_timer ($0330) to $80. The HUD update (UpdateHud) draws the gauge string EnemyGaugeText ([04:336,338]) once, counts the timer down by 2 per frame and erases the gauge when it reaches 0.
engine_spawn_lairs_death_drops:
Actor spawning, then lair, death and drop scripts (file offsets 4783-5393 are batch A1, SNES $00:92AF-$94D1; the scripts from RunLairRespawn on are batch A2 (SNES $00:A6F3 on) and are described in the sections below; the music-load actor MusicLoadSendFade .. MusicLoadFinish and RespawnOrKillActor (file offsets 11419-11622, SNES $00:AC9B-$AD66) are batch A3, see MUSIC LOAD AND RESPAWN at the end).

=== SPAWN PIPELINE (A1 part) ===
Scene load (the scene loader) calls InitActorPool (free-slot stack and pool cleared) and SpawnSceneActors, then the lair code spawns the lair actors. SpawnSceneActors reads world_index ($03BA) and sets $03B0 = offset of the world's meta list inside WorldMetaPointers (the table starts with one list pointer per world, seven in all); it finds the first 4-byte record of ScenePlacementIndex whose area and scene match (the table ends at a first byte of $80 or more) and calls SpawnPlacementList once.
SpawnPlacementList reads 4-byte placement records (bank $01) until a $FF record, allocates an actor for each (PopFreeSlot), links it as the new head and calls InitActorFromPlacement. The actor with $16 bit $0080 is the player: it is placed at warp_dest_x and warp_dest_y + 16 when they are non-zero (anim warp_dest_anim), warp_dest_* are cleared, and player_tile_x/y, player_x/y and player_actor are set.

=== STRUCTURES ===
Placement record (4 bytes, bank $01): x tile, y tile, flags byte (bits 7 and 6 flip Y and X, bit 0 passes to $1C as $0100), meta type. Position = tile x 16, tile y x 16 + 16.
Meta entry (14 bytes at WorldMetaPointers + $03B0 + type x 14): +0 attack, +1 defence, +2 HP, +3 word EXP, +5 animation id, +6 word flags (becomes $16, $8000 added at spawn), +8 word animation table, +A data bank, +B word script, +D script bank.
Lair record (32 bytes in LairRecords, see its note): used by SpawnLairActor: +$C x tile, +$D y tile, +$10 script word, +$12 script bank, +$13 monster count (initial lair state), +$14 spawn interval or formation index, +$15 meta type, +$16 attribute word.

=== NOTES ===
- Names: the lair actor (SpawnLairActor) is the invisible object that runs the lair script and counts the monsters left in $2E and $2F; the monsters it spawns are made by the scripts that follow (batch A2).
- A Monster Lair in the walkthrough loses its shield when its monsters are dead and shows a green switch; the tile $FE written by the lair code is that switch (see lib_scene_map_patches).

=== LAIR SCRIPTS (A2) ===
A lair actor (SpawnLairActor) runs one of six scripts, chosen by the script word of its record (+$10 of LairRecords; the reference counts in OQ-I006-5). All six start with RequireLairTile (the script only runs while the map byte under the lair is $FD, an intact lair, OQ-I006-23), then repeat: COP 91 (entry), wait while the lair is off screen ($16 bit $8000, set by CullAndSortActors), wait while no free actor slot exists (COP 27 retries next frame), BRK #$53, SpawnLairMonster, DelayBetweenSpawns, and SyncLairCount (each frame it compares the monsters left, $2E, with the last value seen, $2F). When $2E reaches 0, SealLair writes tile $FE (the green switch), plays an effect and ends the lair actor.
  RunLairRespawn (156 records): one monster alive at a time; every death makes the lair spawn the next one until $2E is 0. The walkthrough's lairs that 'spit out one at a time'.
  RunLairSpawnAll (139 records): spawns all $2E monsters one after the other (counter in $2C), then only waits for the deaths.
  RunLairFormation (107 records): spawns all monsters at once from a formation list in FormationPointers (index in $26: x, y and flip bits per monster); the monsters skip the appear puff.
  RunLairSpawnAllFlipping (7 records) and RunLairRespawnFlipping (no record, OQ-I006-5): the same patterns, but the lair's flip bits ($1C) step by $4000 after every monster so they alternate orientation.
  RunLairProximity (8 records): waits until the Cop0C test succeeds, spawns one monster, waits for its death, then waits again.
A monster made by SpawnLairMonster starts in RunMonsterAppearPuff (puff, then LoadMonsterFromMeta) and keeps the lair slot in $32; when it dies NotifyLairOfDeath decrements the lair's $2E. lair_state ($7F0203 + lair index) keeps the monster count between scene changes and is set to 0 only when the lair is cleared, so a half-cleared lair starts again with its full count (SyncLairCount).

=== EFFECT PUFFS (A2) ===
RunAppearPuff is the generic 'actor appears' puff, spawned with COP 85 by about 150 scene actor scripts in 137 files; it centres itself on the spawner's box and plays animation 02 of the effects bank ($0E, set by COP A8 #$8000, #0E), or just ends when scene_active is 0. RunHazardPuff replaces the script of a hazard (DestroyHazardsNearOrb) by animation $10 and removal. RunMonsterAppearPuff is the lair monster's first script.

=== ENEMY DEATH AND DROPS (A2) ===
KillTarget and KillOrSpareProjectileTarget (combat) give a killed actor the script RunEnemyDeath. The boss (boss_actor) is diverted to RunBossDeath. For anything else RunEnemyDeath plays the death puff (animation 03), spawns a Gem pickup before itself and shows the EXP earned:
  Drop: w = world_index (world 6 counts as $19). random_mod_result = a random number below $64. t1 = 2w + 1 and t2 = 4w + 4, both doubled when equipped_weapon is 4 (the Lucky Blade; the walkthrough says it yields more Gems than usual, OQ-I006-9). Below t1: RunLargeGemPickup (10 Gems); below t2: RunMediumGemPickup (5 Gems); otherwise RunSmallGemPickup (1 Gem). The pickup is spawned with $16 flags $4000; ApplyContactDamageOrPickup calls ApplyGemPickup when the player touches it.
  EXP number: the BCD word at +3 of the meta entry is drawn as 1-4 digit sprites (the value picks the digit count: below $10, $100, $1000, or more) in a sprite map reached through the pointer table at $7EF000 (slot number x 2); WriteHighNibbleDigit and WriteLowNibbleDigit write the digit tile (ExpDigitTiles) at $7EF005 + X in steps of 7, and the number's x is shifted by +5, +3, +1 or -1 so it stays centred. After $10 frames FinishEnemyDeath runs: with a lair ($32 non-zero) NotifyLairOfDeath counts the death and ends the actor; without one the A3 code at RespawnOrKillActor kills the actor or, when $1A bit $1000 is set, respawns it after $0258 + 1 frames spent off screen.

=== BOSS DEATH AND ENDING (A2) ===
RunBossDeath: $16 = $0700, velocities cleared, contact_lock + 1, the boss box is stored in boss_box_x/y/w/h (position minus the left and upper extents, width and height = the sums of the extents). Then 32 RunBossExplosion actors are spawned, 3 frames apart (COP 03/04 loop); each is placed at a random point inside the box and about half of them play BRK #$85. KillAllOtherActors removes every actor whose $16 has none of the bits $24D0 (the player group and the dying actors stay). At location_id $7D the script jumps (RTS trick) into RunEnding; elsewhere Cop31 spawns the A3 sound handshake actor (MusicLoadSendFade) and the boss ends through FinishEnemyDeath.
RunEnding (SNES $00:D354): shows EndingTextDefeated, then EndingTextStaySingular when souls_flags and $1F is exactly 1 (only the Magician soul, OQ-I006-10) or EndingTextStayPlural otherwise (the singular text jumps into the plural one with [JMP]), clears souls_flags, waits, shows EndingTextWorldFades while RunEndingEffect runs, sets an event flag (COP 09 operand $9F02), writes text_delay ($1B84) = 6 and $031E = 1 and warps with Cop10 to scene 7 of area 0 (OQ-I006-11). KillAllProjectiles is used by the menu code (lib_menus) when the equipped magic changed.

=== PICKUPS (A2) ===
RunSmallGemPickup, RunMediumGemPickup and RunLargeGemPickup play animation 04, 05 or 06, then animation 09, 0A or 0B for a count of 4 (COP 81/83) and remove themselves, so an uncollected Gem disappears. ApplyGemPickup reads the current animation id ($1E): 06 and 0B give 10 Gems, 05 and 0A give 5, 04 and 09 give 1, any other id gives 10 (RunFixedGemPickup, a never-ending pickup with animation 07 spawned by w1_actor_01E4BB, OQ-I006-8). The Gems are added in BCD to gems_low and gems_high by lib_player_stats.AddGems and BRK #$4D is requested.

=== MUSIC LOAD AND RESPAWN (A3) ===
Music load. Cop31 (FadeAndLoadMusic) and Cop32 (StopAndLoadMusic) spawn an actor whose script is the chain below; $30 of that actor is the track number, an index into MusicPointerTable of data_engine_tables (21 long pointers, 3 bytes each). Every step ends with COP 27 or COP 1B, so the steps are one or more frames apart and the game keeps running between them. APUIO0 ($2140) is the CPU-to-SPC port; the command meanings come from docs/audio/spc-disassembly.md (DispatchCommand).
  MusicLoadSendFade: writes $F1 (the SPC's HandleFadeIn handler in that document) and waits (MusicLoadWaitFadeAck) until APUIO0 reads $F1 back, answers with $01 and waits (MusicLoadWaitSilence) until the port reads 0.
  MusicLoadSendStop (Cop32 starts here): writes $F0 (StopAllChannels) and waits (MusicLoadWaitStopped) until the port reads 0, then COP 1B waits 2 frames.
  MusicLoadUpload: writes $FF (the SPC's boot handshake handler), copies MusicPointerTable[$30] to dp$29-$2B and $0422/$0424, waits for vblank, switches NMI off (lib_system_helpers.DisableNmi), runs engine_spc_ipl_upload.code_0FEFF5 (the song data goes through the IPL transfer), waits for vblank and switches NMI on again (EnableNmi); COP 1B waits 2 frames.
  MusicLoadFinish: writes $01, clears boss_fight_active ($0458, incremented by the boss scripts when the fight starts and read by the switch-tile code in lib_tile_triggers_and_lair_return) and kills the actor (COP 86). The meaning of the $F1 / $01 / 0 sequence is inferred from the wait loops (OQ-I025-2); the track numbers used are listed in cop_script_flow_flags (OQ-I025-3).
Respawn. RespawnOrKillActor is the tail of FinishEnemyDeath for enemies without a lair: with $1A bit $1000 clear the actor is killed (COP 86); with it set the actor stays dead until it has been off screen ($16 bit $8000) for $0258 + 1 frames ($26 counts down; on screen the count waits), then InitActorFromPlacement re-creates it in the same slot from its placement record ($3A).
engine_title_file_select:
Title-screen Mode 7 hook and the save-slot (file select) menu (file offsets 27519-28199, SNES $00:EB7F-$EE27, bank 00).

=== MODE 7 (UpdateTitleMode7) ===
HandleVBlank calls UpdateTitleMode7 on every NMI, after FlushVramWriteQueue (engine_vblank_nmi). It acts only when location_id is $10 and returns at once otherwise. The Mode 7 state lives in WRAM: centre m7x_shadow/m7y_shadow ($046A, $046C), scale m7_scale ($0480, written by gv_front_end) and angle m7_angle ($047E, an 8-bit table index; nothing in extracted/ writes it, so the angle is 0 unless a block copy sets it, OQ-I024-4). BuildRotationMatrix builds A = scale * cos, B = scale * sin, C = -scale * sin and D = scale * cos with the PPU multiplier (Mode7Multiply16x8: M7A, a 16-bit scale, times the signed table byte in M7B; the product's middle and high bytes MPYM/MPYH are the result); the tables are SineTableTail (cos) and SineTable (sin), $40 entries apart, a quarter turn of 256 steps. The results go to m7_matrix_a-d ($0476-$047C). WriteMode7Matrix then writes the shadows (m7a_shadow-m7d_shadow, m7x_shadow, m7y_shadow, $046E-$0474 and $046A-$046C) to M7A-M7D, M7X and M7Y (each write-twice register gets the low byte, then the high byte), and UpdateTitleMode7 copies the new matrix into the shadows, so the PPU always shows the matrix of the previous NMI. RefreshTitleMatrixAlt and BuildRotationMatrixAlt (an alternative matrix routine) have no caller (OQ-I006-6).

=== FILE SELECT ===
EnterFileSelect is reached by BRL from gv_front_end. It calls lib_01232B.code_01232B, draws the menu and continues in HandleFileSelectChoice (COP 1B). DrawSaveSlotMenu prints the heading (gv_title_texts.SaveSlotMenuText), then checks the four slots at $700000 + n * $400: lib_save_system.ComputeSlotChecksum computes the checksum of the slot into dp$16/$18 and compares it with the words at +$3FA and +$3FC. A valid main block is copied over its backup mirror at +$1000 ($3FE bytes, MVN); an invalid one is restored from the backup and checked again; a slot that is valid in neither is not listed. For every listed slot the menu line is filled from the save block ($1B92 + offset: five fields into $0447-$044E, $1B6A + offset into $0450, $1B90 + offset into $0452) and printed with lib_text_render.PrintTextString. If no slot is valid the last-used slot word $701FFE is set to 0. HandleFileSelectChoice starts the cursor at $701FFE (slot 0-3, else 0), asks lib_0118FC_part2.ChooseMenuRowAtTable, and treats an answer of 4 as a second prompt (probably erase: it stores the slot offset into the first word of the main and backup blocks and switches the palette word $7F0006 from $7FFF to $03FF while it runs, OQ-I024-5). Any slot 0-3 is stored in save_slot, loaded with lib_save_system.LoadGameFromSlot and the game warps: scene_next = 1 when the load reports carry (inferred: no valid save, a new game) or the word at $1B90 of the loaded save otherwise, with warp_dest_anim = 1 and the player at x $70, y $60.
engine_unreferenced_code:
Code that nothing in the ROM calls (file offsets 517-833 and 29873-29906, bank 00).

=== DEBUG BLOCK (offsets 517-833, SNES $00:8205-$8341) ===
DebugPollPad2 and its helpers have no caller and no vector entry: a pad 2 poll (Select: scan banks $00, $03, $04 and $1F for the bytes 02 01 AA followed by a word of $8000 or more; B: wait 30 frames; Y: show a hex position readout), a hex digit helper pair and table, and DebugApplyItem (a two-digit BCD item entry in $0484 that nothing writes). They look like leftover debug code; that is an inference, not proven (OQ-I005-22 asks for a CDL run). us/overrides.json forces M = 1 at offsets 517 and 797.
DebugShowPosition writes hex digits into the text buffer $1F06-$1F1A (area, scene, location, tile x, x low digit, tile y, y low digit, actor count) and prints it from $1F02 through the text renderer PrintTextString; the template at $1F02-$1F05 is never initialised.

=== UnusedAnimWaitStep4 (offset 29873) ===
UnusedAnimWaitStep4 (SNES $00:F4B1) is an unreferenced actor script: it plays animation 07 (COP 80, COP 82) in a loop until $0482 = 4, plays 07 once more, then animations 08 and 09, increments $0482 and ends with COP 91. $0482 is the step counter of the gv_front_end sequence (written and read only there and here), and the routine lies between two of that file's INC $0482 sites, so it looks like an unused step of the title sequence (OQ-I006-7).
engine_vblank_nmi:
NMI handler and the DMA routines it calls (file offsets 834-1444, SNES $00:8342-$85A4, bank 00).

=== ORDER OF WORK IN HandleVBlank ===
Saves P, B, A, X and Y; works with M = 1, X = 16-bit, DBR = $01. HDMAEN = 0; then DmaOamBuffer, DmaCgramAndFixedColor, DmaBg3TilemapPage, WriteScrollRegisters, UploadMapStripBuffers, DmaDynamicSpriteTiles, DmaAnimatedTileStrip, FlushVramWriteQueue and the title and file-select hook engine_title_file_select.UpdateTitleMode7; then wait for the auto-joypad read (HVBJOY bit 0); HDMAEN = dp$42 (the shadow the work phase set); frame_counter++; joypad; sound request. DMA channels: 0 = OAM, 1 = CGRAM, 2 = every VRAM transfer.
HandleIrq (the IRQ vector) is a bare RTI; the I flag is never cleared (no CLI in extracted/), so the IRQ stays masked.

=== JOYPAD ===
JOY1L is read as one word. The X button (word bit 6) is copied to the Select position (bit 13), so X and Select act as one button. joy_pressed = raw buttons with the bits of joy_block_mask removed (scripts block buttons with TSB and TRB on joy_block_mask), ANDed with joy_release_latch: a button counts only while its latch bit is set. The latch gets a bit whenever that button is seen up; the users (player code, menus, level up) clear the bit with TRB after using a press, so a held button acts once. Scene init sets the latch to $FFFF. joy_override ($0468) non-zero skips all of this and keeps the scripted value in joy_pressed (used by the Lisa and Turbo scene).

=== SOUND ===
sound_request ($0398, word) is filled by the BRK handler (HandleBrk): BRK #n requests sound n. On even frames the word goes to APUIO2 and is cleared; on odd frames 0 is sent.

=== STAGING DATA THE NMI UPLOADS ===
- oam_buffer $0486: 512 bytes low table + 32 bytes high table (544 bytes, channel 0 to OAMDATA).
- palette $7F0000 (512 bytes, channel 1 to CGDATA); COLDATA from coldata_buffer $7F0200-$7F0202.
- BG3 tilemap pages: $7F7000 to VRAM $5800, or (bit 1 of vram_upload_flags) $7F7800 to $5C00, 2048 bytes each.
- Scroll words: BG1 from scroll_bg1_x/y ($033A, $033C), BG2 from scroll_bg2_x/y ($033E, $0340), each value 10 bits (low byte, then high byte and 3); bg_scroll_swap ($03DB) non-zero swaps the pairs. BG3 uses the low bytes of scroll_bg3_x/y.
- Map strip records at $3000, $3102 and $3204, $3306 ($102 bytes each; column record, then row record).
- tile_dma_list $1A06: 3-byte records (source address word, bank), 0 ends; tile_dma_pending is the trigger.
- vram_strip_src, vram_strip_dest, vram_strip_pending ($03DD, $03DF, $03E1): one animated background strip.
- vram_write_queue $1C7B: pairs of words (VRAM address, data), address 0 ends.
player_core:
The player: spawn script, input filter, action choice, per-frame motion finish, push zones, corner slide, Gem pull and return-trip facing, together with the 28 pose handlers, the four swings, PayPhoenixCost, PublishPlayerAnim and the four Phoenix projectiles (file offsets 5394-8143 and 9848-9959, SNES $00:9512-$9FCF and $00:A678-$A6E7, bank 00). The blade layer, soul orb, spells and level-up of the same hero are in player_spells_level_up.

=== ONE ACTOR, FIVE HELPERS ===
The hero is one actor per scene, created from the first record of the world's meta table (WorldMetaPointers: seven identical entries with animation 0, $16 = $1180, animation table PlayerAnims and the script InitPlayerActor). InitPlayerActor stores its slot in player_actor, selects the sprite tile source $7F:3000 (COP A9) and clones five helpers, each of which starts as a copy of the player: WatchForLevelUp (COP 84), RunSoulOrb (84; it spawns RunSoulOrbController), FilterPlayerInput (84), FinishPlayerMove (85) and RunWeaponLayer (85). Run order inside a frame: WatchForLevelUp, RunSoulOrb, RunSoulOrbController, FilterPlayerInput, the player, RunWeaponLayer, FinishPlayerMove. So the controller reads joy_pressed before the filter strips B and Y (spells work without a weapon), and it sees the position that FinishPlayerMove published in the previous frame.
With return_active set (the scene is entered from a stored return point: return_area, return_scene, return_x, return_y and the switch record return_record) InitPlayerActor spawns only the level-up watcher and the hero becomes FacePlayerTowardReturnTarget: no orb, filter, weapon layer or camera follow. Every scene load builds the full set again.

=== ANIMATION STEPS, NOT FRAMES ===
An actor script resumes when its countdown $14 underflows. COP 82 steps the animation and the actor yields for the step duration plus one frame; the engine applies the step velocity ($04 dx, $06 dy) every frame. So the player script runs once per animation step, not once per frame: a walk cycle is six steps, and the first step of every walk handler moves 2 px per frame in all four directions (static reading, OQ-I032-15). The idle animations $00-$03 are one step of duration 0, so while the hero stands the script runs every frame and decides again at once. Whatever has to react between two steps (a released key, the sword button) must cut in from outside: that is the job of FilterPlayerInput, which writes ChoosePlayerAction into the resume pointer $18.
Direction codes are the game's own: 0 up, 1 down, 2 right, 3 left for the facing (PlayerFacingByAnim) and for the movement direction (PlayerMoveDirByAnim). The idle animations $00-$03 are the poses facing down, up, left, right.

=== CHOOSING THE ACTION ===
ChoosePlayerAction runs after every animation. A dying hero ($16 bit $0400) goes to PlayPlayerDeath. With no weapon or in a no-combat scene the unarmed path is used, otherwise the armed path. Plain walking is a direct branch (Right, Left, Down, Up in that priority; BRL StartWalkRight and so on). Everything else goes through PlayerActionTable: 44 rows (one per animation $00-$2B) of 6 handler addresses, slot 0 = B (armed only), 1 = Right, 2 = Left, 3 = Down, 4 = Up, 5 = no key. The table path is taken when L or R is held, when B is held (armed), or when no direction is held (idle).
The rows depend only on the facing of the current animation, except the twelve rows $14-$1F (all StartIdleUp). So the table says: keep the facing, choose the pose of the pressed key. With L or R held the hero keeps his facing, which is the crab-walk of the walkthrough (02-grass-valley.md: 'press and hold the L or R Button to basically move sideways', with a sword also a thrust). Pressing a direction without L or R turns him that way.
The carry on entry to a handler picks between the two animation ids of the paired handlers: clear = pose family $00-$13 (unarmed, or armed with L or R held: the thrust, the blade stays out); set = armed without L or R, pose family $24-$2B (sword carried). The sword hurts only while the animation is below $24 (ApplySwordHit).

=== MOTION ===
FinishPlayerMove runs after the player: the push of a conveyor or wind (ScanPushZones reads an 8-byte record list: x0, x1, y0, y1 tile bounds, dx and dy words in pixels per frame, a first byte of $FF ends the list; 13 lists and 54 records in the game, 52 of them move 1 px per frame and two in St. Elles 4 px), else the corner slide, an even-pixel snap, the published position, the blade layer and the camera. The conveyor belts are in Grass Valley (walkthrough chapter 2), the wind in Magridd's Castle (chapter 7: 'the wind on the ship will be pushing you back').
SlideAroundCorner lets the hero slide 2 px along a wall into a gap when his key is held and he is not tile aligned on the other axis. PullGemsToPlayer pulls Gems toward a hero who stands still with the sword out and L or R held (the thrust idle).

=== NOTES ===
- Walkthrough: crab-walk and thrust with L or R (chapters 1 and 2), the minimum level of a weapon applies to the B swing but not to thrusts (items.md), conveyor belts (chapter 2) and ship wind (chapter 7). The walkthrough does not name the hero (you choose a name), so the notes say 'the hero'.
- An earlier reading called PullGemsToPlayer a 'sword push-back scan'; the code moves pickups toward the hero and touches no enemy (OQ-I032-1).
- Dead or unexplained: SlideUnusedReturn is an unreferenced RTS; AnimKeepKeyMask words $14-$23 are never read; animations $14-$1B and $1D-$1F are protected by the filter but nothing identified plays them (OQ-I032-2).
- Bank limits: every JSR inside the file is a 2-byte reference, so the filter, motion and Gem routines must stay in bank 00 with their callees; PlayerActionTable holds 2-byte handler addresses, so the table and the handlers share bank 00.
player_spells_level_up:
The hero's blade layer, soul orb, magic and level-up: RunWeaponLayer, RunSoulOrb and RunSoulOrbController, the spell gate DispatchSpellCast, the seven spells with their child actors, EndSpellActor and the level-up watcher with its 'LEVEL UP !' blink (file offsets 8143-9848, 9959-9971 and 12118-12293, SNES $00:9FCF-$A678, $00:A6E7-$A6F3 and $00:AF56-$B005, bank 00; the four Phoenix projectiles between them belong to player_core). All of it is spawned by InitPlayerActor.

=== BLADE LAYER AND SOUL ORB ===
RunWeaponLayer is a clone of the player with $16 and $CEFF (visible, no tile collision, not-a-hit-source bit cleared) and the animation bank $0B changed to $0C, so it plays the blade sprites of WeaponOverlayAnims while the body plays PlayerAnims. FinishPlayerMove puts it on the player every frame.
RunSoulOrb stays hidden ($16 bit $2000) while return_active is set or souls_flags is 0, then shows the orb: the walkthrough says the Soul of Magician 'also ends up being the little orb of light surrounding you'. It spawns RunSoulOrbController, which moves an invisible steering point and writes the orb's position every frame: the d-pad moves the point 2 px per frame per axis whether or not the hero can move, a pull toward the hero adds 1 px (2 px at 80 px or more distance to the right or below, 96 px to the left, 64 px above), and the orb sits on a circle of radius 31 px around the point (the sine tables SineTable and SineTableTail, index soul_orbit_phase x 2 mod 256, sample / 4, so 128 phases per turn at one phase per frame). The orb can be parked in front of enemies; spells start at the orb. The walkthrough: a soul reveals hidden passages in King Magridd's Castle 'as your orb of light circles over them'.

=== SPELLS ===
DispatchSpellCast is called by the controller every frame. With no spell alive and Y pressed, equipped_magic - $11 picks the arm; each arm pays with COP 26 (BCD Gems, halved by Magic Armor, zero with the Magic Bell; too poor: nothing is cast), increments spell_active_count and spawns the cast actor with COP 85.
equipped_magic: spell (ROM text and walkthrough magic.md agree), Gems, cast actor, damage byte $30 of the projectile (ApplyProjectileHit reads it):
$11 Flame Ball, 4 Gems, RunFlameBall, 5. $12 Light Arrow, 8, RunLightArrow (four arrows), 10 each. $13 Magic Flair, 8, RunMagicFlair, 20. $14 Rotator, 1 per burst, RunRotator, 5 per burst. $15 Spark Bomb, 8, RunSparkBombSpawner (four bombs), 30 each. $16 Flame Pillar, 20, RunFlamePillarSpawner (four pillars), 6. $17 Tornado, 8, RunTornado, 15. $18 Phoenix, 2, not here: the sword swings cast it (PayPhoenixCost).
Every cast actor copies the orb's position at its first run and plays animations of bank $0F (COP A8 #$8000, #$0F = MagicAnims); the movement is in the animation steps (velocity words per step), not in the scripts. $16 values: $03A0 = harmless while it forms (projectile $0020, not a hit target $0200, not yet a hit source $0100), $02A0 = armed (bit $0100 cleared), $2020 = hidden projectile of a spawner, $0010 added = runs in sub-frames. The Flame Ball goes in the facing direction (PlayerFacingByAnim; the opposite directions use the flip commands COP 96 and 98), the Light Arrow in all four, Magic Flair is charged by holding Y (tap plus three levels: animations $0D/$10, $0E/$11, $0E/$12, $0E/$13), the Rotator releases a burst every 5 frames while Y is held, the Spark Bomb and Flame Pillar spawners drop four actors about 18 frames apart, and the Tornado wanders in a four-state heading graph (see RunTornado).

=== THE CAST LOCK ===
spell_active_count counts the live spell actors and is tested first by the gate, so no spell at all can be cast while one lives (the walkthrough only says one Tornado is allowed: OQ-I032-7). The Flame Ball, Light Arrow, Magic Flair and Rotator actors end through EndSpellActor, which clears the count and consumes the Y press (TRB $4000 of joy_release_latch: a held Y does not cast again); the Flame Ball clears the count already at the launch. The Spark Bomb, Flame Pillar and Tornado parents reset the count to 0 and let their children INC / DEC it; the last one to end consumes the press. The gate also refuses when the free actor stack ($4A) is empty.

=== LEVEL UP ===
WatchForLevelUp loads the EXP needed for the next level from LevelExpThresholds[player_level x 4] (two big-endian BCD words, the first one is the high word) and compares it with player_exp as a 32-bit subtract. At 50 it ends. On a level: max HP and HP + 2 capped at 100, COP 37 refills the bar over time, player_level and player_level_bcd + 1, the new level's low bit chooses level_defense (odd) or level_power (even) + 1, the HUD is marked dirty, BRK #$97, then 'LEVEL UP !' (LevelUpText) is printed three times for 21 frames each with 11 frames of blank (LevelUpClearText) between, and the watcher checks again, so a big EXP gain gives several levels in a row.

=== NOTES ===
- Walkthrough checks: the seven Gem costs, the four-arrow Light Arrow, the three charge levels of Magic Flair, one Tornado, the Rotator's 1 Gem per burst, the level cap of 50, max HP + 2 per level (8 at level 1, 100 at level 47), strength at even and defense at odd levels, and four EXP table rows (level 1 = 100, level 2 = 280, level 18 = 83,000, level 19 = 115,000) agree with the code. The ROM spells the third spell 'Magic Flair' as the walkthrough does.
- DISCREPANCY, Spark Bomb: the walkthrough says four bombs at sixty-degree intervals, the fourth 180 degrees from the first; the code spaces them about 18 frames apart at 2 of 256 sine steps per frame, about 51 degrees each (OQ-I032-3).
- DISCREPANCY, strength and defense: the walkthrough caps the unequipped values at 13 and 12; level_power and level_defense have no cap here, and lib_menus clamps only the display of the level parts to 12 (OQ-I032-8).
- The Tornado's first heading and every restart use LDA #$0302, an immediate that is always 2 (OQ-I032-6).
WorldMetaPointers:
Actor meta tables: the 7-word world pointer table and the seven lists of 14-byte actor types, 469 entries in all (file offsets 32768-39347, SNES $01:8000-$99B3, bank 00; 6580 bytes).

=== MODEL ===
Every actor placed in a scene, every lair monster and the player is an instance of a meta type: one 14-byte row that gives its stats, first animation, animation table and script. There is one list per world (world_index 0-6: Grass Valley, GreenWood, St. Elles, Mountain of Souls, Leo's Laboratory, Magridd's Castle, World of Evil), so a type number means something different in each world: type $1F is the Metal Mantis in world 0 and a Mini Race Car in world 4. SpawnSceneActors stores the offset of the world's list in $03B0; every consumer reads its row at WorldMetaPointers + $03B0 + type x 14 (listings show $&WorldMetaPointers+N,Y with DBR $01 or $81). The type number comes from a placement row (+3, the PlacementAaaSss lists) or from a lair record (+$15, LairRecords).

=== ENTRY LAYOUT (14 bytes) ===
+0 attack, +1 defence, +2 HP (a binary byte), +3 word EXP (BCD), +5 animation id, +6 word flags (becomes $16; $8000 is added at spawn), +8 word animation table, +A animation bank, +B word script, +D script bank. +8..+A is the 3-byte Address field of structs.json and +B..+D the @Code field. Damage (comments in the combat code): the player's hit on a monster is max(1, attack_current - monster defence (+1)); a monster's hit on the player is attack (+0) - 1 - defense_current, at least 0. The EXP word is added in BCD by KillTarget and drawn as digits by RunEnemyDeath.
HP is binary and EXP is BCD: the bestiary values of docs/walkthrough/enemy-bestiary.md match this reading for every enemy that could be matched (for example Metal Mantis 50 HP and 50 EXP = bytes $32 and $0050).

=== WHAT THE OPERANDS SAY ===
Animation table (+8..+A): 358 of the 469 entries use $7E3800 (the sprite map the scene loader expanded into WRAM: the step lists of ordinary actors travel with the scene), 69 use PaletteAnimLists (bank $0D, the colour animations: mostly types $01-$0F of every list, 14, 14, 13, 15, 5, 3 and 5 types in worlds 0-6; none of the enemies), 7 use PlayerAnims (entry 0 of every world, the hero), 4 use EffectAnims and 31 have $000000 (the actor selects its own table with COP A8). Flags word (+6): $2010 95 times, $2040 87, $0040 49, $0000 43, $2048 39, $2050 38, $1000 22, $3040 21 and 28 more values with fewer entries.
Entry 0 of every list is the hero: attack 1, defence 2, HP 3, animation 0, flags $1180, table PlayerAnims, script InitPlayerActor. The seven copies are identical (the stats are not used; the player's own stats live in the $1B.. fields).

=== ENEMY TYPES (matched by stats) ===
The ROM names nothing. The part notes of the seven lists name the enemy types by matching HP and EXP against the walkthrough bestiary (inferred). Where the bestiary gives several enemies the same stats the ids cannot be told apart this way and the note says so. The four bosses whose ROM HP differs from the bestiary, the world 6 Purple Bull and the types that match no bestiary row are OQ-I033-1 to OQ-I033-4.

=== NOTES ===
- The names MetaGrassValley .. MetaWorldOfEvil label the list starts; a type number is the index of a row inside its list, so type $1F of world 0 is MetaGrassValley + 31 x 14.
- engine_0026F3.code_00296A loads +5 as a word (so the low byte of the flags becomes the high byte of the animation id): harmless for rows whose flags low byte is 0 (OQ-I014-5).
